passages.text: In the ordinary course of study, I fell upon a certain book of Cicero, whose speech almost all admire, not so his heart. This book of his contains an exhortation to philosophy, and is called "Hortensius." But this book altered my affections, and turned my prayers to Thyself O Lord; and made me have other purposes and desires. Every vain hope at once became worthless to me; and I longed with an incredibly burning desire for an immortality of wisdom, and began now to arise, that I might return to Thee.
passages.note: A book that changes one's purpose and desires

passages.text: But Thou wert more inward to me than my most inward part; and higher than my highest.
passages.note: God closer than one's own self
